page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v6 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. A key characteristic of this configuration is its high memory-to-compute ratio, providing 256.0 GB of RAM alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. In addition to high-capacity system memory, the instance includes 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations show competitive single-threaded capabilities alongside expected scaling constraints from the 8-vCPU allocation. The instance scored 2051.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, placing it in the top 25%, while multi-core evaluations like stress-ng reached 7988.69 and Geekbench multi-core reached 7780.0, both within median thresholds. In-memory and caching metrics demonstrate 11.06 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and cached memory read bandwidth of 621.92 GB/sec. Large uncached memory operations measured 66.17 GB/sec for reads and 45.13 GB/sec for writes. PassMark memory testing was relatively constrained at 1716.72, and medium-scale LLM generation (7B model) reached 8.29 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of discrete GPU accelerators.

By limiting compute to 8 vCPUs while retaining a 256.0 GB memory footprint and 1890 GB NVMe SSD scratch space, the E32-8ds_v6 offers targeted licensing efficiency for software products priced per core. The architecture avoids excessive licensing costs while satisfying substantial memory and fast ephemeral storage demands. Workloads matching this profile include core-licensed relational databases, in-memory data processing, caching tiers, and data analytics pipelines requiring high RAM density.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Single-threaded performance is strong, verified by a Geekbench single-core score of 2051.0, while multi-core output reflects its constrained core count. Memory bandwidth ranges from 66.17 GB/sec on uncached reads to 621.92 GB/sec for cached 16KB blocks, supporting 11.06 million Redis SET operations per second. With 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance offers high resource density for per-core licensed databases, memory-resident data stores, and analytical workloads.
